A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and describe the same BOP-Ask dataset, pipeline and main experiments. v1 includes Appendices A–C; v3 ends after the references. This omission is directly observable, rather than an extraction gap.

before.justification: v1 reports original VLM evaluations, fine-tuning experiments, human annotations, ablations, dataset analyses and physical robot results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark and fine-tuning results, the human study, ablations and the robot task-completion comparison, despite omitting the appendices.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same world-frame construction, RRT trajectories, M2T2 grasp generation and question-generation procedure. The fine-tuning approach also remains unchanged. Removing Appendix A reduces implementation disclosure without establishing an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Training sources, six interaction tasks, BOP-Ask-core/lab, transfer benchmarks and robot tasks remain unchanged. The removed Appendix B eliminates supplementary corpus-analysis coverage, including BLINK spatial questions and SpatialBench position questions; this does not imply that the retained VLM evaluations changed.

E2.justification: The VLM and human comparator sets in the main experiments are unchanged. However, Appendix B/Table 7's dataset-quality comparison against RoboSpatial-Home, BLINK and SpatialBench disappears. Newly cited Robo2VLM and ManipBench are not added experimental baselines.

E3.justification: The retained experiments use the same splits, model sizes, metrics, hardware and human-study design. Removing Appendix B also removes its lexical and semantic evaluation protocol, including vocabulary, type-token and referential-complexity measures. Missing robot success thresholds are lost documentation, not evidence of revised robot trials.

E4.justification: v3 removes the dedicated dataset-diversity and question-complexity analysis in Appendix B, together with the real-robot execution case studies in Appendix C/Figure 6. These are substantive losses of supplementary analysis. Table 5's data-recipe ablations and Figure 3's qualitative comparisons remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same averaging of human responses, including multiple annotations for roughly 30% of questions. Neither reports model-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The removed Table 7 question-length standard deviations describe corpus variability, rather than experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: Main numerical results remain unchanged, including zero versus ten completed robot tasks out of fifteen. However, v3 removes Table 7's corpus statistics and Table 8's base/SFT robot scores: grounding 24.4/73.8, grasping 16.7/74.0 and trajectories 0/71.4. These and the removed robot execution examples constitute substantial lost supporting results, not changed same-setting performance.

T1.justification: The sample definition, world-frame mathematical formulation and normalized coordinate error equation remain unchanged. Neither version presents theoretical propositions or proofs. The omitted appendix material supplies implementation and empirical-analysis details rather than additional mathematical theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: approximately 150k images and 33M question-answer pairs, six tasks including four claimed novel tasks, two benchmarks, and improved interaction reasoning and transfer after fine-tuning.

C2.justification: v3 loses Appendix B's interpretation of compositional diversity and Appendix C's specific unseen-object generalization discussion and failure attribution to object misidentification. The main interpretations concerning geometric supervision, clutter, transfer and rearrangement difficulty remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Omitting Appendices A and C removes unique reproducibility details: SAM 2 segmentation, calibration refinements, collision checking, the 3 cm path-simplification tolerance, example answer formats, robot success criteria and controller settings such as 20 cm execution height and 5 N grasp force. The abstract also drops the explicit dataset-and-pipeline release promise while retaining the project link; actual external availability cannot be established from these PDFs.

R1.justification: v3 adds Robo2VLM and ManipBench to the related-work citations and bibliography. The surrounding positioning and comparisons with prior spatial-reasoning and robotics research remain substantially unchanged; most reference-number changes merely reflect these additions.

P1.justification: The removal of all three appendix sections substantially contracts the document's explanatory structure, especially the pipeline and robot-execution exposition. Main-text editing is otherwise limited to small wording changes, redirecting the pipeline reference from Figure 4 to Figure 2, and expanding acknowledgments and funding information.

P2.justification: v3 removes Tables 6–8 and Figures 4–6, including the pipeline diagram, question-answer examples, corpus statistics, word cloud, task-distribution chart and robot execution montage. Main Tables 1–5 and Figures 1–3 retain their content, with limited text reflow and footer changes. The removed task-distribution chart repeats proportions still available in Table 2.

improvement.justification: v3 preserves the main claims and scores but removes unique dataset-construction and robot-execution details, success criteria, component-level robot results and supporting examples. This substantially weakens reproducibility and scrutiny of the real-world manipulation evidence; the text still refers to supplementary material absent from the supplied v3 PDF. Small editorial fixes and two added citations do not offset these losses.
